_comment: OWH taxonomy (D-014 plus .claude/planning/asset-storage-policy.md). Reusable art is placed by semantic geography and category before the owning family; level placement never owns a reusable asset.

lint._family_patterns_comment: One entry per route in the destination table, most specific first. The table mixes depths on purpose: a building kit is one ownership family behind Buildings/Kits, while an environment pack owns its family directly under the category.
lint._assembly_patterns_comment: A building kit exists to be assembled from parts, so its outgoing family references are the artifact working, not decay. Measured 2026-08-15: 164 of the 177 edges into Buildings/Parts came from one kit, which is why Parts is not a shared library and the kit is not an offender. The direction that does cost something - reaching into a kit's internals - is reported as depends-on-assembly.
lint._rule_severity_comment: Shared reaching into a private family is the rule that makes Shared meaningless, so it stays an error. Family-to-family is a warning with a register: the migrated library already carries such edges by construction, and turning them into a hard stop would only get the lint disabled.

_routes_comment: One rule per route in .claude/planning/asset-destination-table.json, most literal first: the resolver prefers the template that pins down more segments, so a route naming Buildings/Kits beats the generic library route without ambiguity. Each route comes in two shapes - with a canonical type folder and without - because a family may hold its assets flat or split them by type (owner, 2026-08-17). The typed shape is listed first so PlaceAsset answers with it; the flat shape stays for reading paths that already exist. A type folder is only ever one of the names in kind_directories: anything else is pack residue and must stay unmatched so the audit can see it.
